findings.title: AMD security bulletin AMD-SB-6009: Radeon Graphics kernel driver privilege management vulnerability (CVE-2023-20598)
findings.summary_md: AMD's vendor advisory, initial publication 2023-10-16 per its Revisions table, describes CVE-2023-20598 in the Radeon Software kernel driver pdfwkrnl.sys: improper privilege management lets an authenticated attacker craft an IOCTL to gain I/O control over arbitrary hardware ports or physical addresses, potentially yielding arbitrary code execution. It credits Takahiro Haruyama of VMware with the report and sets fixes at Adrenalin Edition 23.9.2 (23.20.11.01, 2023-09-19) and PRO Edition 23.Q4 (23.30.13.03), covering Radeon RX 5000/6000/7000 cards and Ryzen 6000/7000-series processors with Radeon graphics.

findings.title: NVD record for CVE-2023-20598
findings.summary_md: NVD published the CVE-2023-20598 record on Oct 17, 2023 with CVSS 3.1 7.8 HIGH (AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H): improper privilege management in the AMD Radeon Graphics driver allows a crafted IOCTL to gain I/O control over arbitrary hardware ports or physical addresses. Affected configurations list Radeon Software Adrenalin up to (excluding) 23.9.2 and PRO up to (excluding) 23.Q4 across RX 5000/6000/7000, Radeon PRO W5000-W7000, and Ryzen 6000/7000-series iGPU platforms; the linked vendor advisory is AMD-SB-6009.

findings.title: The Hacker News: researchers catalogue 34 vulnerable Windows drivers including PDFWKRNL.sys (CVE-2023-20598)
findings.summary_md: This November 2023 article covers VMware Carbon Black researcher Takahiro Haruyama's study of 34 Windows drivers with firmware access through port I/O and memory-mapped I/O, explicitly naming PDFWKRNL.sys (CVE-2023-20598) among them. It notes six of the drivers allow kernel memory access that can be abused to elevate privilege and defeat security solutions, foreshadowing the exact BYOVD use Lunex applies to the driver.

findings.title: BlueTeamCoolTeam: original ClickFix/CAPTCHA campaign analysis dropping the Lunex Rust stealer
findings.summary_md: Luke Wilkinson's June 10, 2026 post documented the ClickFix/CAPTCHA campaign three months before the story's September window: the lure page at captcha-code[.]lol delivered a five-layer RC4-plus-gzip PowerShell loader that dropped the Lunex infostealer, a Rust binary that force-installed a malicious browser extension, enumerated active Windows logon sessions via LSA APIs, and performed Active Directory user and group reconnaissance. The C2 in that sample was 94.154.32[.]21:8080.

findings.title: BlueTeamCoolTeam: OSINT into a live Lunex stealer C2 panel network
findings.summary_md: Posted June 12, 2026 and updated June 14, this Shodan-and-Validin investigation confirmed six live Lunex C2 panels on port 8000 across the US, Finland, Germany, the Netherlands, and Ukraine, with the first panel deployed 2026-05-14, plus a Cloudflare-hidden panel at api-goo-drivehosting[.]com registered 2026-06-05 to imitate Google API traffic. It published the Lunex favicon MD5 b9251db3aa9511157cba432c0b5402fc for infrastructure hunting and showed the panel supports JavaScript injection, content spoofing, screenshots, and full remote browser control, not just credential collection.

findings.title: Public pdfwkrnl.sys exploit repository for CVE-2023-20598
findings.summary_md: The GitHub repository unkvolism/pdfwkrnl, described as 'pdfwkrnl.sys exploit', was created on 2025-12-22T23:06:42Z, nine months before the September 2026 campaign. The Hacker News' September 26, 2026 Lunex report links this repository as the privilege-escalation code path for CVE-2023-20598, meaning public, working exploit code for the AMD driver predates the observed abuse by roughly nine months.

findings.title: The Hacker News: hacked Ukrainian sites serve fake Cloudflare ClickFix lures for Psychedelic Stealer (Arctic Wolf Labs report)
findings.summary_md: Published 2026-09-24T19:59:00+05:30 (14:29 UTC, 36 minutes before the story's first_seen), this was the first coverage of the September campaign, summarizing Arctic Wolf Labs' technical report: compromised Ukrainian business sites injected iframes loading fsputnik[.]com/tds/tracker.js, the fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA copied an msiexec command fetching elita.msi from uasputnik[.]com (registered September 9, 2026), and the payload psychedeliclove.exe reported to C2 193.178.159[.]128:8080. The exposed Rublevka TDS lure panel recorded 557 views, 426 clicks, and 79 complete events across 32 countries, 446 of the views from Ukraine.
